findings.decompiled: call newOwner.transferOwnership(address newOwner) with: / gas gas_remaining / args Bytes(28, uint128(newOwnerWallet >> 32)), Bytes(4, uint32(newOwnerWallet))
findings.issue: The single address argument of the call is printed as two slices of the same value (28 bytes of newOwnerWallet >> 32, then its low 4 bytes), because the encoded word sits at an offset of 4 from a 32-byte boundary.
findings.rule: Adjacent argument slices Bytes(a, x >> 8b) followed by Bytes(b, Mask(8b, 0, x)) with a + b = 32 are the word x; print one argument x.

findings.decompiled: const owner = 0 / if caller: revert with NotOwner()
findings.source: address public immutable owner; if (msg.sender != owner) revert NotOwner();
findings.issue: The immutable owner reads as 0 before deployment.

notes: Tiny proxy, read in full. executeDelegateCall: the bytes argument is copied to memory twice (the decoded _data and the call buffer); the call is printed directly from calldata ('args data[all]'), so the two memory copies are dead in the text (P8); the revert bubbling of 'result' and the bytes return are correct. No loops.
summary: Faithful; the only oddity is one call argument printed as two slices of the same address, plus the zero immutable owner.
